clusters.name: Accurate representation of the reasoning process
clusters.description: An explanation or chain of thought is faithful when it accurately represents, reflects or describes the process by which the model reached its output; the cluster also holds the taxonomies that divide this umbrella into kinds of test and the conditions papers set on any faithfulness measure.

clusters.name: Disclosure of the factors that drove the answer
clusters.description: A trace is faithful when it states the factors (cues, hints, biases, concepts) that actually moved the answer; includes the cue tests, their judges, labeling rules, cue taxonomies and failure modes such as unverbalized hint use.

clusters.name: Causal dependence of the answer on the stated reasoning
clusters.description: A trace is faithful to the extent that the answer depends on it: truncating, corrupting, paraphrasing, replacing, unlearning or patching the reasoning should change the answer; post-hoc reasoning is the central failure.

clusters.name: Agreement between the stated reasoning and the answer
clusters.description: Faithfulness read off the output: the answer follows from, is entailed by or agrees with the stated reasoning, including faithful-by-construction systems and validity-based definitions.

clusters.name: Say-do consistency: actions against the stated reasoning, plan or claim
clusters.description: What a model says it will do, has decided or has done is compared with what it does: plan-execution gaps, thought-action consistency, claims about completed actions against tool logs, stated choices against tool actions.

clusters.name: Predictive value: the explanation lets an observer predict the model
clusters.description: An explanation is faithful if a reader (human, simulator or listener model) can use it to predict what the model does on the same or related inputs: simulatability, LAS, counterfactual simulatability, NSG, rationale utility.

clusters.name: Self-report accuracy: the model's reports about itself
clusters.description: A model's report about its own policy, dispositions, learned behaviors, confidence, internal states or counterfactual behavior is faithful when it matches what the model does or what is inside it; includes introspection, privileged access and grounding.

clusters.name: Input importance: the explanation marks the inputs the prediction depends on
clusters.description: Feature-attribution faithfulness: the inputs an explanation marks as important are those whose removal or alteration changes the prediction, or the inputs driving the prediction also drive the explanation.

clusters.name: Correspondence with internal computation
clusters.description: Faithfulness checked against internals: a CoT step is faithful if it describes a process that took place in the model, as shown by probes, attribution graphs, circuits, SAE concepts or activation readouts.

clusters.name: Honesty and dishonesty: statements against the model's own beliefs
clusters.description: Statements judged against what the model believes or knows: lies, deception, honesty rates under pressure, confessions and admissions of misbehavior, and truthful reasoning chains.

clusters.name: Companion notions defined by contrast
clusters.description: Companion terms defined to say what faithfulness is not: plausibility, self-consistency, consistency with gold labels or across inputs, effectiveness, truthfulness, informativeness, interpretability, monitorability.
